gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Ink strokes that taper off before they touch give this body a light, approachable hand. Noto Sans Tai Le keeps a long page of text easy on the eye, while Origami's brush-lettered heading carries the personality up top.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Origami paints every stroke at a constant width, like a sign-painter's single pass of the brush. And Noto Sans Tai Viet follows with a tall x-height and short ascenders, so a long stretch of text stays easy to take in.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-takri: Brushed lettering, dense as poured lead, then a lowercase that hikes its waistline up. Noto Sans Takri leaves its small round letters generously unclosed, and the two sit together with a bold, flat heading above and a light, open body below.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Contemporary through and through, with a brush-drawn heading that never tapers. Noto Sans Tamil is the sharper quality here: its text looks magnified at any size, with terminals stopping well clear of the stem, which makes Origami look even more solid beside it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tamil-su: Stocky, rounded and quietly bold, with Origami's lowercase massed like poured lead. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement has round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall the line looks sturdy, which makes a long passage feel dense but friendly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Brush-painted lettering with a skimming ease, set against a body with wide, inviting round openings. Noto Sans Tangsa keeps a long read relaxed.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tc: Origami looks like a sign-painter's brush pulled at constant width, with thin joins as sturdy as the stems. Noto Sans TC does the opposite job: its tall, large-countered letters and outward-opening curves are built for reading, where Origami is built for being looked at.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Origami has the flat, stencil-like weight of a sign painter's brush. Noto Sans Telugu sets a high midline and counters that stay connected to the outside, so a longer stretch of text moves along with little friction.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Wide channels lead into each counter of Noto Sans Thaana, so its big open lowercase forms read with real ease. And Origami sits above it with strokes as steady as a drawn string, a flat, brushy heading over a roomy body.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-thai: Origami draws stems like dowels and arcs like bent dowels, a sign-painter's brush at constant width. Noto Sans Thai follows with a lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads and rounded letters left open, so a long page feels soft and approachable.
